summary: The natural-timing probe ran (CheckRun c839d00a425a4b75b09fbfb353fc4fc8, exit 0) and returned the no-fall branch: 792 fast-path deliveries, all successful, each followed immediately by a term sample, zero falls, and a term that climbed monotonically to 2390 in memory and in the stable store. That is the honest and expected outcome for a window a couple of instructions wide, and it bounds the finding rather than refuting it. The absence is meaningful because a term is only ever written in this implementation as the current term plus one or as an adopted higher term, so a fall would have been unambiguous; the sampler therefore did not miss it, the interleaving simply did not occur in this run. I recorded the observation with its operands, stated the resulting bound as order-of-magnitude rather than as a calibrated rate, since a rule-of-three style reading of zero events in 792 opportunities puts the per-delivery probability below roughly a fraction of a percent, and named the caveat that my deliveries were bursty rather than uniformly distributed in time. I kept the defect claim where the evidence is, on the two witnesses and the causal control, and did not upgrade this negative into either a refutation or a claim that the hazard is common. I also registered the schedule and configuration dependence as the open question, and recorded a mechanism insight that narrows it: a denser delivery schedule is partly self-defeating, because every delivered heartbeat refreshes the follower's last contact and restarts the election timer it is trying to catch, so pushing harder postpones the campaign instead of landing more writes inside it. The promising direction is therefore the one that lengthens the election's read-modify-write interval, such as a multi-voter cluster or a slower stable store, rather than higher delivery density. The six witnessed findings, the reproduced and controlled regression, and the two knowledge corrections remain recorded and unaffected.
